root_cause: The datepicker component (via vanilla-calendar-pro's inputMode keyboard handling) intercepts Tab keydown on the input element and calls preventDefault(), blocking default browser focus movement to the next form field. The previous fix used a bubbling-phase listener which runs after VCP's handler, so preventDefault() had already been called.
repair_strategy: Add a capture-phase keydown event listener on the input element that detects Tab key, stops propagation to prevent VCP's handler from running, hides the datepicker calendar if shown, and allows default browser behavior (focus movement) to proceed without preventDefault. Clean up the listener on dispose.
expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key now moves focus from departure date field to passengers field as expected in standard form navigation, restoring keyboard accessibility for form traversal per WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.3.
functional_risks: Minimal - only affects Tab key behavior on datepicker input elements
Arrow key navigation within calendar remains intact
Capture-phase listener runs before VCP's handler, preventing its preventDefault()
verification_requirements: Arrow keys still navigate calendar dates when open
Escape still closes calendar (existing regression guard)
Form submission works with entered values
